title: Zenexa - POC scoping (open-model shortlist & benchmarks)
summary: POC scoping focused on selecting a small set of open models to evaluate for a multilingual customer support summarization and routing POC. Discussed quality vs cost tradeoffs, target SLAs, dataset sizes for benchmarks, EU data residency, and pilot timeline. Agreed next steps: share benchmark template, propose 3-model shortlist with quantized variants, and schedule a focused latency/cost benchmark next week.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-20 14:00 PT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Recording: Auto-recorded
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Priya, Luca, Amira, Noah (Zenexa), Samir joined later

Summary (auto): POC for multilingual support summarization/routing, shortlist open models, set benchmarks and timeline

00:00 Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining on time, quick intro from our side, maya — ae at redwood, diego is our se who will run the benchmarks
00:18 Priya: Hi thanks, i'll kick off, our goal is a 6 week POC to see if open models can hit our summarization quality and latency targets, also need EU residency
00:32 Diego: got it, just to clarify do you mean both summarization and routing to specialized teams?
00:38 Priya: yes, two capabilities; short abstractive summary and routing label (3 classes: billing, tech, escalation). Must support en, it, ar (english, italian, arabic)
00:55 Amira: adding product note — cost sensitivity, we need to keep hosted costs under a target, but willing to consider dedicated if quality difference is substantial
01:10 Luca: technical constraints: current infra is AWS eu-west-1, latency target for interactive UI is 500ms p95 for inference end-to-end, we expect bursts up to 120 concurrent requests
01:30 Maya: ok makes sense. for the POC we'll propose model variants (multilingual vs domain-tuned) and quantized profiles. typical shortlist we see: Llama-2-70B (quantized), Mistral-7B-instruct / Mixtral-8x if you want smaller/faster, and MPT-30B or Falcon-40B as an intermediate — we'll put pros/cons
01:55 Priya: curious on multilingual — Llama-2 is good but we've seen italian fine, arabic is hit or miss; any multilingual-focused models you recommend?
02:10 Diego: right, for arabic we sometimes prefer models with explicit multilingual pretraining or instruction-tuning; we can include XLM-R based variants or a multilingual LLM like Llama-2 multilingual forks; also evaluating Mistral variants which have decent non-english perf
02:30 Noah: security questions up front — can the POC run in our VPC? we need KMS integration and audit logs
02:40 Maya: yes, Redwood Private supports VPC/private control plane and KMS/HSM; for POC we can run on Dedicated capacity with VPC peering or do a host+VPN option, we'll share the security pack
02:58 Priya: success criteria: we propose primary metric = summary quality F1 / ROUGE-ish or human eval > 0.8 of baseline (current in-house extractor) and routing accuracy > 90%; secondary metrics latency p95 < 500ms and cost under $0.03 per call — happy to adjust
03:20 Diego: good to make them numeric; for bench we typically run both automated metrics + 200 human eval samples per language to catch edge cases
03:36 Amira: timeline? 6 weeks sounds tight, what are the realistic phases?
03:44 Maya: typical POC phases: week 0 gather data + access, week 1 setup + baseline runs, week 2-3 model tuning and quantized testing, week 4 human eval + bench, week 5-6 decision + wrap-up. we can compress some steps if you provide data quickly
04:05 Luca: workload sizing — our average ticket length is 250 words, median 120, so sequence lengths for bench should be capped at 512 tokens; daily volume for POC simulated runs ~10k messages/day, but for benchmarks we'll simulate bursts of 120 concurrent clients
04:25 Diego: on the runtime side we need to pick batching & kv-cache strategies; for short messages batching helps throughput but hurts tail latency; we'll test batch sizes 1, 4, 16 during the benchmark
04:40 Priya: model quantization — we want to test 8-bit vs 4-bit — trade off on quality is the big unknown
04:48 Diego: yes; we'll include 8-bit and Q4 variants where available; Redwood Optimize can recommend quant profiles based on sequence distribution
05:00 Maya: let's talk shortlist specifics. SE suggestion: (1) Llama-2-70B q8 and q4 variants — high quality but heavier; (2) Mixtral/Mistral-7B-instruct q8 — good cost/perf for european languages; (3) MPT-30B-instruct q8 or Falcon-40B-instruct as a balanced option. we'll include an additional smaller baseline like Mistral-3B to gauge cost floor
05:30 Priya: ok include a domain-tuned variant if you think it's worth it; we might want to try a light fine-tune on 5k tickets if results look close
05:45 Diego: fine-tune plan: we'll do a 1-2 epoch lightweight instruction-tune on your anonymized tickets; cost/time estimate in the pilot doc
06:00 Amira: benchmarking: what metrics will you run automatically?
06:06 Diego: automated: ROUGE/ROUGE-L, BERTScore for semantics, routing accuracy confusion matrix; latency p50/p95/p99, throughput, and cost per 1k calls. Human: 200 samples per language for quality judgment (3 raters)
06:26 Priya: human eval logistics: can redwood run it or we do internal?
06:30 Maya: we can run it or provide the template and you run it; many customers prefer we do the split and provide anonymized results
06:42 Noah: for compliance, we need SOC 2 docs + encryption in transit & at rest details. also retention policy — POC data must be deleted after 90 days unless agreed
06:55 Maya: we'll send security pack and SOC 2 evidence; deletion policy can be enforced and we can provide audit logs
07:08 Luca: can you share expected cost ranges for each model per 1k calls? ballpark fine for planning is ok
07:15 Maya: rough ballpark: Mistral-7B q8 ~ $1.50 per 1k calls, MPT-30B q8 ~ $4 per 1k, Llama-2-70B q8 ~ $12 per 1k (variable by batch and token length) — will provide more accurate numbers in pricing doc
07:40 Priya: those numbers help. if 70B is high we might do a canary on a subset of VIP users and run cheaper model for the rest
07:55 Diego: yes routing policies can fall back to a cheaper model for low-risk tickets and use higher-quality for escalation
08:10 Amira: for multilingual, we should prioritize italian first then arabic since volume is EN > IT > AR; but include AR in bench because critical tickets sometimes come from Arabic users
08:25 Priya: agree. also please include transliteration cases and mixed-language inputs in the sample set
08:40 Samir: (joined) sorry late — brief question on infra: do you support autoscaling for burst traffic in Dedicated?
08:48 Maya: yes, dedicated pools can autoscale within configured limits and we can set burst capacity for short spikes, we'll detail config options
09:00 Diego: ok next technical step: we'll prepare a benchmark plan that exercises q8/q4, batch sizes, and model switches; run plan will include 3 runs per model variant and aggregated metrics
09:20 Priya: how long does a run take?
09:24 Diego: each run for the 10k simulated messages should be ~20-30 minutes depending on concurrency and model size; total bench time for all variants ~6 hours, but can be parallelized across multiple GPU nodes
09:40 Maya: wrap-up recap: Redwood to send benchmark template + security pack by fri 5/22, SE to propose 3-model shortlist + quant variants by mon 5/25, zenexa to upload anonymized tickets by sun 5/24, schedule bench for week of 5/25. action owners noted.
09:58 Priya: sounds good, thanks everyone
10:02 Amira: thanks, we'll review and revert on priorities
10:10 Meeting end
